name: memory_read
description: START HERE — call this FIRST at the beginning of every task to recall what you already know before doing any work (never re-derive or re-explore facts that may already be saved). Reads memory fragments. SUMMARY MODE: shows title + description only (not full content). Use id parameter to get full detail of a specific fragment. Use all=true to see fragments from all projects.

project.description: Project name to filter (optional, defaults to detected project)

query.description: Optional semantic search keyword. Supply only if you are looking for specific context.

id.description: Get FULL DETAIL for a specific fragment ID. Use this after seeing the summary to read the complete content.

context.description: Optional context tag for this access (e.g., 'debugging', 'refactoring'). Boosts confidence and tags the fragment for future recall.

all.description: If true, show fragments from all projects. Default: false (current project + global only)

ids.description: Get full details for multiple fragment IDs at once. Optional.

minConfidence.description: Minimum confidence threshold (0-1). Only return fragments with confidence >= this value. Optional.

afterDate.description: ISO date string (e.g., '2026-04-01'). Only return fragments created on or after this date. Optional.

beforeDate.description: ISO date string (e.g., '2026-04-30'). Only return fragments created on or before this date. Optional.

limit.description: Max fragments to return per page (default 30, max 100). Only applies in browse/search mode, not for id/ids. Optional.

offset.description: Number of fragments to skip for pagination (default 0). Use next_offset from the previous response to fetch the next page. Optional.

response_format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default, human-readable) or 'json' (machine-readable structured payload). Optional.

expand_graph.description: When reading a specific fragment (id), also surface related fragments reachable through its relations (bounded traversal: depth ≤ 2, strongest links first). Default: false. Optional.

explain.description: Opt in to why each returned memory was selected in THIS call, with recorded sources and evidence freshness. Default false. Does not reconstruct a past recall. Evidence files are checked only if verification.stale_check is enabled; confidence is not proof of correctness. No corrections are applied automatically.

count.description: Number of fragments returned in this response.

fragments.description: Matching memory fragments (summary fields, or full content for id/ids).

related_graph.description: Fragments reached via relations when expand_graph is set (id, title, depth, score).

has_more.description: Whether more results are available beyond this page.

next_offset.description: Offset to pass for the next page, if has_more is true. Null when there is no further page.

name: memory_add
description:
MANDATORY: Call this AFTER completing analysis/research to save findings. Synthesize information into short, reusable fragments.

FRAGMENT SCHEMA — always follow this structure:
## [Topic Title]

### Context
[1-2 sentences: what and why it matters]

### [Content Section]
- [Key fact 1]
- [Key fact 2]

### Rules (optional, for patterns/warnings)
- [Absolute constraint]

RULES:
- ALWAYS store fragments in ENGLISH regardless of conversation language. This ensures search and retrieval works correctly.
- Title: max 80 chars, start with topic name
- Fragment: 30-2000 chars, structured markdown, NOT plain prose
- Every fragment MUST have a ## heading and at least one ### section
- Type: Choose based on nature:
  * fact = technical info, API behavior, version details
  * pattern = repeated solution, best practice, code pattern
  * lesson = learned from experience, mistake, debugging insight
  * warning = caution, gotcha, pitfall to avoid
  * context = environment info, project setup, dependencies
- Auto-title: If you omit title, first 40 chars of fragment used
- Auto-description: First sentence extracted from fragment

fragment.description:
The memory fragment text to store. Follow this format:
## [Topic Title]
[1-2 sentences of context: what and why it matters]
- [Key fact 1]
- [Key fact 2]
- [Constraint or note if any]
Keep fragments between 30-2000 characters. Use structured markdown, not plain prose.

title.description: Short title for the memory (auto-generated if not provided). Max 80 characters.

description.description: Short description/summary (auto-generated if not provided). Max 150 characters.

project.description: Project scope. Omit to auto-file under the current project (detected from cwd). Pass 'global' or null for cross-project scope.

confirm.description: Set to true to store fragment as-is even if secrets are detected. Default: false (auto-redacts).

type.description: Fragment type. 'fact'=technical info, 'pattern'=repeated solution, 'lesson'=learned from experience, 'warning'=caution/gotcha, 'context'=environment info. Default: 'fact'.

evidence.description: Optional code backing for this fragment. Cite the file and the exact snippet it was derived from; an opt-in recall check later flags the fragment if that snippet drifts. Windows-safe, no embeddings.

file.description: Path to the cited source file.

symbol.description: Optional symbol/function/section label the snippet belongs to.

snippet.description: The exact code snippet the fragment is based on (stored verbatim + SHA-256).

id.description: ID of the newly stored fragment.

conflicts.description: Detected conflicts against existing fragments, if any.

name: memory_update
description: Update an existing memory fragment by ID. Can update title, fragment text, confidence, or all.

id.description: The ID of the fragment to update

name: memory_feedback
description: Provide feedback on a memory fragment after use. positive = the memory was useful (boosts confidence), negative = it was not helpful (reduces confidence by -0.1).

id.description: The ID of the fragment to give feedback on

useful.description: true if the memory was helpful, false if it was not relevant or incorrect

id.description: ID of the fragment receiving feedback.

name: memory_forget
description: Remove a memory fragment by ID. Pass consolidate=true to archive (down-weight, keep, reversible), or invalidate=true to hide it from recall while preserving its content and version history (reversible), instead of hard-deleting.

id.description: The ID of the fragment to remove

consolidate.description: If true, archive the fragment (down-weight to 0.05 so recall ignores it) instead of deleting it — non-destructive and reversible. Default false (hard delete).

invalidate.description: If true, logically invalidate the fragment: hidden from recall entirely but kept in the DB with its full version history, and reversible. Use for superseded/outdated facts you may want to audit later. Takes precedence over consolidate. Default false.

name: memory_merge
description: Merge multiple memory fragments into one. You decide the merged content, this tool just executes the merge. Use when you find related/overlapping fragments that should be consolidated. Pass consolidate=true to supersede+down-weight the sources (reversible) instead of deleting them.

ids.description: Array of fragment IDs to merge (will be deleted after merge)

project.description: Project scope. Omit to auto-file under the current project (detected from cwd). Pass 'global' or null for cross-project scope. Optional.

consolidate.description: If true, keep the source fragments but mark them superseded by the merged one and down-weight them (non-destructive, reversible) instead of deleting. Default false.

id.description: ID of the new merged fragment.

merged_ids.description: IDs of the source fragments that were deleted.

name: memory_relate
description:
Create a typed relation between two memory fragments. Bidirectional — reverse relation auto-created.

RELATION TYPES — when to use each:
- supports: Fragment A reinforces/validates Fragment B
- contradicts: Fragment A contradicts/invalidates Fragment B
- supersedes: Fragment A is newer and replaces Fragment B
- related_to: General connection between fragments

WHEN TO CALL:
- After memory_add if you know this relates to an existing fragment
- After memory_update if content changed significantly
- After discovering two fragments are connected during analysis

relation.description: The relation type that was created (bidirectional auto-reverse applied).

name: memory_stats
description: Get memory store statistics: fragment counts, average confidence, project breakdown, and health metrics.

project.description: Project name to filter stats (optional, defaults to all projects)

response_format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default, human-readable) or 'json' (machine-readable structured payload). Optional.

name: memory_audit
description: Audit memory store for integrity issues: orphan references, duplicate IDs, confidence anomalies.

response_format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default, human-readable) or 'json' (machine-readable structured payload). Optional.

issues.description: Human-readable integrity issue descriptions (orphans, duplicates, anomalies).

healthy.description: True if no issues were found.

name: memory_library
description:
Library Mode: Analyze and organize your entire memory database. Returns a comprehensive snapshot with all fragments, guides, relations, pre-computed analysis signals (stale, duplicate, orphan detection), and suggested actions. After reviewing the snapshot, use other tools (memory_merge, memory_forget, memory_update, guide_distill, memory_relate) to execute organizational changes.

WHEN TO CALL:
- Periodically to maintain a clean, well-organized knowledge base
- When memory feels cluttered or redundant
- After a long project with many fragments added
- To find distill candidates that haven't been promoted to guides

project.description: Filter to a specific project. Omit to analyze ALL projects.

focus.description: Focus area. 'full' = complete snapshot (default). Other values return only relevant sections.

limit.description: Max fragments to return per page (default 50, max 200). Optional.

offset.description: Number of fragments to skip for pagination (default 0). Optional.

response_format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default, human-readable) or 'json' (machine-readable structured payload). Optional.

signals.description: Pre-computed analysis signals (stale, duplicate, orphan detection).

relations.description: Relation graph summary: total, by_type, isolated_fragment_ids, hub_fragments.

suggestions.description: Suggested organizational actions as human-readable strings (null when none).

has_more.description: Whether more fragments are available beyond this page.

name: semantic_search
description: Search memories using TF-IDF semantic similarity. Finds related memories even when different words are used. Unlike FTS5 keyword search, this understands topic similarity. Use when keyword search fails to find related knowledge.

query.description: The text to find semantically similar memories for.

project.description: Filter to a specific project. Omit to search all.

topK.description: Maximum results to return per page (default 10, max 30).

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination (default 0). Use next_offset from the previous response to fetch the next page. Optional.

hybrid.description: Opt into hybrid retrieval: fuse BM25 keyword ranking with TF-IDF similarity (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), rerank by recall priority, and diversify results (MMR). Better recall on mixed keyword+concept queries. Default: false (pure TF-IDF).

explain.description: Opt in to why each returned memory was selected in THIS call, with recorded sources and evidence freshness. Default false. Does not reconstruct a past recall. Evidence files are checked only if verification.stale_check is enabled; confidence is not proof of correctness. No corrections are applied automatically.

response_format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default, human-readable) or 'json' (machine-readable structured payload). Optional.

results.description: Semantically similar fragments with similarity scores.

has_more.description: Whether more results are available beyond this page.
